extractor.note: Read every paragraph carrying transcend- (outside transcendental) or immanen-, in file order. No stratum is set: the commentary works text by text and the record does not assign texts to the 1917 and 1918 stays.

coverage_note: Term-led pass over the whole file (lines 1-969): every paragraph containing the transcendence family, including bare transcendent and immanent, was read; paragraphs without such a word were not read. Most occurrences are the technical "immanent time-object"; only places where immanence or transcendence does work are recorded.

units.claim: The editors report that the earlier texts call sensations immanent time-objects, distinguished from transcendent objects in objective time.
units.quote: Sensations are called "immanent time-objects" in the earlier texts, distinguished from transcendent objects in objective time (e.g., a violin tone).

units.claim: As a transcendent object constitutes itself in the apprehension of a sensation-datum, so sensation constitutes itself in absolute consciousness as an immanent time-object.
units.quote: Just as a transcendent object constitutes itself in the apprehension of a sensation-datum, so sensation itself constitutes itself in "absolute" consciousness as a (present, past, or future) immanent time-object.

units.claim: The flow of absolute retentional consciousness has a double intentionality, one transverse intentionality directed at immanent time-objects and one longitudinal intentionality of self-reference.
units.quote: The flow of "absolute" retentional consciousness thus harbors a double intentionality: one directed at immanent time-objects ("transverse intentionality" / Querintentionalität) and one having the form of self-reference or self-consciousness of the flow

units.claim: Husserl distinguishes immanent from transcendent time and states that all egos, constituted as mutually transcendent, have the same time-modality and stand in the same Now.
units.quote: All egos (constituted as mutually transcendent) simultaneously have the same modality of time, stand in the same Now.

units.claim: Where perception is taken as an act-objectivity in immanent time, immanent has the Ideas sense of relation to adequately given objectivities in an adequately given time-form, and the argument against unchanging perception fails.
units.quote: "Immanent" here has the Ideas sense: relation to the unity of adequately given objectivities in an adequately given time-form.

units.claim: The immanent perception does not properly constitute the perceived but is a correlative unity of immanent time, and immanent temporal objectivity itself points back to the primal process.
units.quote: The immanent perception is not what properly constitutes the perceived but is a correlative, essentially belonging unity of immanent time.

units.claim: In pure immanence no plurality of subjects is first given, so immanent time comes first, then the constitution of an objective non-immanent time, then intersubjective time.
units.quote: So first we have immanent time, then the problem of constituting an "objective" non-immanent time, then a time constituting foreign and own consciousness as human, intersubjectively identifiable.

units.claim: Even for immanent objects the constituted unity can never be a piece of the constituting consciousness; the real hyletic datum is a component of consciousness, not of the conscious object.
units.quote: Even for immanent objects, the constituted unity of consciousness can never be a consciousness-piece in the constituting consciousness.

units.claim: Outer perception is a continuous course of inner perceptions of immanent temporalities, through which a second intentionality constitutes the outer object in its transcendence and objective time.
units.quote: outer perception is in its essence a continuous course of "inner" perceptions (perceptions of immanent temporalities), through which a second intentionality runs, constituting the outer object in its transcendence and objective time through "representation."

units.claim: Immanent perceiving can no longer be called apprehending in the sense of outer perception, since no deeper constituted object lies beneath the sensation-datum.
units.quote: He considers whether immanent perceiving can itself be called apprehending—but in the same sense, no longer: there is no concrete consciousness with a still-deeper constituted object lying beneath the sensation-datum.

units.claim: The being of immanent objects is inseparable from the being of their constituting process, unless that process is a last primal process conscious of itself.
units.quote: their being is inseparable from the being of their constituting process

units.claim: Within the discussion of phenomenological idealism, the perceivability of transcendent objects does not require that they be immanent, and spatial objects can be without being actually perceived.
units.quote: The perceivability of transcendent objects does not require that they be "immanent." Spatial objects can be without being actually perceived.

units.claim: The diagram shows the constitution both of the time-stretch of the event and of the sequence of constituting experiences of the second transcendence-level.
units.quote: but also the sequence of constituting experiences of the second transcendence-level

units.claim: A purely hyletic environment as first immanent temporal objectivity co-develops with the lowest-level ego up to the empirical ego that has a transcendent objective world over against it.
units.quote: the latter up to the empirical ego that has a transcendent objective world over against it

units.claim: Everything in the pure consciousness-stream can change within filled immanent time except the ego, which is the necessary immanent individuality.
units.quote: It is the necessary immanent individuality.

units.claim: For mediately constituted physical spatial objects, immanent time serves as apprehensive representative, and through it an objective apprehended time accrues.
units.quote: When objects are mediately constituted (e.g., "physical" spatial objects), immanent time serves as apprehensive representative — and through this representation, an "objective" apprehended time accrues.

absences.expected_because: The section holds the objectual apprehension identical across perception, retention, recollection and phantasy, the point at which Part III separates the transcendent object from the immanent data that represent it.
